acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.presentation: Sun 6/21 AM basketball: minor right-calf pull played through, then acute severe left-calf pain ('shot with a lacrosse ball'), difficulty bearing weight since. Classic acute medial gastrocnemius strain ('tennis leg'), at least Grade II given the can't-weight-bear onset.
acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.selfScreenJun23: Later 6/23: no swelling or bruising, calf symmetric, and the Thompson/Simmonds calf-squeeze test normal and symmetric (foot plantarflexes both sides). Complete Achilles rupture now much less likely (Boyd 2015 PMID 26622031); DVT lower probability given no swelling/asymmetry (Wells 1997 PMID 9428249). Working dx: acute medial gastrocnemius strain, likely Grade I-II.

ruleOut.test: Achilles tendon rupture - Thompson/Simmonds calf-squeeze test
ruleOut.reason: THE can't-miss diagnosis. Rupture patients can still walk and weakly plantarflex and may have no palpable gap, so it is missed unless the squeeze test is done. A radiological 'partial tear' is treated as complete until proven otherwise (Boyd 2015 PMID 26622031; Maffulli 1998 PMID 9548122, squeeze-test sensitivity 0.96).

ruleOut.test: DVT assessment - Wells score +/- Doppler ultrasound
ruleOut.reason: DVT is found in ~10% of tennis-leg presentations and can mimic or be masked by a strain. Red flags: disproportionate unilateral swelling, warmth, redness, calf >3 cm larger than the other side (Delgado 2002 PMID 12091669; Wells 1997 PMID 9428249).

If pain is out of proportion to exam with a tense/firm compartment and pain on passive stretch, seek emergency care - these are early signs; pulselessness/pallor are late (Pechar & Lyons 2016, DOI 10.1016/j.nurpra.2015.10.013).

acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.imaging: Ultrasound (first-line) or MRI to confirm location, grade, and aponeurotic/intramuscular-tendon involvement, which predicts a longer return to sport (Green 2020 PMID 33030961; Meek 2022 DOI 10.2106/JBJS.RVW.21.00183).

ptHomeProgram.reconciliationWithTheProgram: The PT's prescription is now the calf and single-leg rehab line, and the program stops writing a parallel one so the two do not stack. Three consequences. FIRST, the program's 3x/week seated calf HSR at 135 (3x8, run as 3x10 on 7/28) retires in favor of the PT's daily 3x15. Daily calf loading is a legitimate evidence-supported pattern, closer to Alfredson's 180-heel-drops-daily model than to Beyer's 3x/week HSR, and the two produced equivalent 12- and 52-week outcomes (Beyer 2015; Strong), so this is a different protocol rather than a worse one. THE DOSE IS BODYWEIGHT, confirmed by what was actually performed on 7/29. The program initially assumed a 90 lb anchor, which was invented rather than prescribed and has now been corrected everywhere. This matters because unweighted 3x15 is a much lighter calf stimulus than 3x8-10 at 135, so retiring the loaded line is a real de-load of loaded calf capacity rather than a like-for-like swap. ASK THE PT whether bodyweight is meant to stay or to progress; if it stays, the loaded single-leg raise below becomes the only loaded calf work in the week. SECOND, the loaded single-leg calf raise at BW+25 is NOT in the PT's program even though they know about it. It is kept at once weekly rather than dropped, because at roughly 1.11x bodyweight it is the only thing in either program that addresses the >=1.0x BW knee-extended strength benchmark gating return to sport (Green 2022 PMID 35032233), and a bodyweight hold does not reach that strain. Flag it for the PT and defer if they want it out. THIRD, daily step-backs off a box with a forward chest lean are controlled stair-descent loading, which supersedes the program's own more conservative note that there should be no heel drop below neutral until stair descent is pain-free. That gate was the program's, the PT's judgment is more current, and theirs governs. The single-leg RDL also replaces the Glute-Ham Raise / Ham Curl line for hamstring volume: hip-dominant, single-leg, calf-sparing, and it exposes left versus right.
openQuestions: What grade is the strain, and did anything get measured?
What load do they intend for the daily seated calf raise 3x15 and the single-leg RDL 3x8?
Do they want the BW+25 loaded single-leg calf raise to continue?

Do they agree with the hop and capacity criteria (~20 symptom-free single-leg hops, >=30 calf raises at <=10% asymmetry) as the gate for running, plyos, and a return to basketball, or do they have their own return-to-sport criteria? If they have their own, theirs govern.

nutritionGoals.primary: Steady fat loss preserving lean mass, strength, and game performance
nutritionGoals.rationale: Apr 20 body-comp overview showed +4.7 lbs fat / +1.9 lbs lean over 6 weeks. Initial 2-day/week deficit-at-BMR approach (set Apr 20 AM) was recalibrated later that day based on Helms 2014 and Aragon 2017 ISSN evidence: (1) rest-day target at BMR was more aggressive than needed, (2) intermittent restriction is not superior to daily small deficits per ISSN 2017, (3) weekly deficit was below the Helms 0.5%/wk floor anyway. Revised to moderate-deficit across 3 non-heavy-training days.

goals.name: Moderate-deficit days
goals.weeklyDeficitEstimate: ~900-2,100 cal/week = ~0.3-0.6 lb/week fat loss (within Helms 2014 0.5-1%/week lean-preserving range)
goals.rationale: REVISED 8/4 for the current week shape. Tue = rest day, PT calf block only, no lifting and no game since basketball is in its off-season. Wed = upper body only, no lower-body demand, which is the exact rationale that used to justify Thursday. Sat = pre-Sunday-game rest day, PT block only. Mon and Thu carry the barbell lower work and the graded run and stay at maintenance to fuel it; Sun stays at maintenance as the game day. SUPERSEDES the Mon/Thu/Sat scheme, whose rationale had gone stale in every clause: it read Mon as a no-training recovery day when Mon now carries the heaviest session of the week, it held Tue at maintenance as a game day when there is no Tue game, and it anchored the deficit around a Wed heavy TB DL that has moved. Daily deficit of 300-500 cal below TDEE preserves lean mass per Helms 2014.
goals.evidence: Helms et al. 2014, JISSN (PMID 24864135): 0.5-1% BW/week loss rate for lean-mass preservation in resistance-trained athletes. Aragon et al. 2017 ISSN position stand (PMID 28630601): intermittent restriction not superior to daily small-deficit approach.
goals.revisedNote: Anchor days moved Mon/Thu/Sat to Tue/Wed/Sat on 2026-08-04 (Wk 22 science review) to match the post-injury week shape.

goals.name: Restaurant meal cap
goals.rationale: Hall 2019 ward study (Cell Metab) showed ultra-processed/restaurant food environments drive ~+500 cal/day spontaneous intake vs matched whole-food diets. Current pattern: 5-7 restaurant meals/week consistently drives 3,000+ cal days. Capping at 3 fixes the weekly caloric creep without daily macro tracking.

supersededGoals.name: Deficit rest days (original Apr 20 AM)
supersededGoals.supersededReason: Target was at BMR (~1,990 cal) which was more aggressive than needed. Math using rest-day TDEE (~2,400) showed actual deficit was only 300-400 cal per day = 600-800 cal/week, below the Helms 0.5%/week floor anyway. Revised to gentler 3-day approach.

dailySupplements.evidenceTier: Emerging for tendinopathy. Shaw 2017 (PMID 27852613) showed 15g gelatin/collagen + ~50mg vitamin C 30-60 min pre-loading doubles collagen synthesis biomarkers in serum. Praet 2019 (PMID 30609761) RCT used FORTIGEL specifically for achilles tendinopathy and found symptom improvements. Momentous formulation matches both protocols (15g + 50mg vit C, FORTIGEL inclusion). Optimal timing: 30-60 min PRE Wed/Fri HSR sessions for tendon-specific adaptation. Post-game/post-loading timing has weaker evidence but still contributes to general recovery.

activityLog.activity: Power Red (Double Red Cell) blood donation
activityLog.details: Apheresis donation, AM. Two units of packed red cells removed; plasma and platelets returned with saline. Logged as a physiological event for load context, not as a training or recovery session.
activityLog.notes: Power Red removes ~2 units of red cells (roughly double a whole-blood donation), lowering hemoglobin/hematocrit and oxygen-carrying capacity. The early hit has two clocks: a blood-volume loss that plasma re-expansion resolves in ~3 days, and a red-cell-mass deficit that takes weeks. Whole-blood RCTs show maximal power, VO2peak, and Hb mass still depressed up to ~4 weeks post-donation, with the sharpest acute VO2max drop (~15% at 2h, ~10% at 2d, ~7% at 7d) right after (Meurrens 2016 PMID 27873242; Hill, Vingren & Burdette 2013 doi:10.1139/apnm-2012-0361). Iron strongly speeds blood/Hb recovery (REDS-III, Kiss 2015 PMID 25668261) and, for a repeat donor like him, limits cumulative performance decline across donations (PMID 32931412); it does NOT fast-forward single-donation performance recovery, which returns in ~1 wk regardless. Full sourcing in knowledge/blood-donation-recovery.md. Because Power Red removes ~2x the red-cell mass, expect a longer return than the ~3-4 wk whole-blood window - the Red Cross 112-day Power Red deferral vs 56-day whole blood implies plan ~4-6+ weeks to baseline aerobic capacity. Iron loss is also ~2x. Evidence tier: Moderate (controlled performance data is whole-blood; the DRCA-specific timeline is extrapolated from those RCTs plus the regulatory deferral). Material because Phase 3 power-realization opens Wk 15 this week and 6/14 is a basketball-AM/hockey-PM double on a depleted system.

BOTH BARBELL LOWER LIFTS CAME BACK IN ONE SESSION: TB DL 4x5x205 clean, and back squat pulled forward from Friday, ramped 45/95/135 and held 135 for two sets. That is a materially bigger first session back than the plan called for, and the 40-day layoff makes it the highest-uncertainty session of the block. Both restarts landing clean is the expected outcome rather than a surprise: strength decays much more slowly than muscle size, so the first sessions back typically go better than they feel like they will (Psilander 2019 PMID 30991013, where CSA returned to baseline after 20 weeks off while strength stayed roughly 60% elevated; Moderate). The same trial found no faster retraining in a previously trained limb, so this is strength retention, not muscle memory. TB DL has one clean session banked and a second clean 4x5x205 earns +10 to 215. The squat does NOT: two working sets at 135 is not a clean 4x5, so Friday repeats 135 and aims for all four sets. No deload gets stacked on the far side of a layoff. CALF WORK DIVERGED FROM THE PLAN, UNDER CLINICAL DIRECTION: isometric standing calf holds were added (6x30s bilateral plus 3x30s per leg single-leg, 4.5 min of total hold time), seated calf raise ran 3x10 at 90/135/135 (two more reps per set than prescribed, same load shape as 7/8), and the loaded single-leg calf raise was SKIPPED along with the hamstring work. The isometric holds were PT-PRESCRIBED, part of the home program from the morning visit, so this was clinician-directed rather than freelanced. Isometrics are the Phase 1 modality in the consensus progression (Green 2022 PMID 35032233), and collagen signaling responds to strain magnitude rather than contraction type (Kjaer 2009; Magnusson and Kjaer 2019), so they contribute real stimulus. The single-leg holds also expose left versus right qualitatively. What a bodyweight hold cannot do is reach the >=1.0x BW knee-extended strain of BW+25 loaded work or produce a countable rep number, so it satisfies neither gate criterion. Do not credit isometrics with analgesia either: Rio's findings are patellar-specific and Achilles replication is mixed (Rio 2015 PMID 25979840; Weak for Achilles generalization). Total calf load for the session was therefore HIGHER than prescribed, not lower, which is the load-management question worth watching rather than any concern about the movements chosen. Calf silent during the session (0/10). MORNING-AFTER READ (7/29 AM): 1-2/10 diffuse soreness, well inside the pain rule of up to 5/10 during loading and the next morning, settling to baseline within 24 h and not climbing week to week (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888). That is a genuinely good tolerance signal for a session this size, with the caveat that so many simultaneous changes mean a bad read could not have been attributed to any single load. CAPACITY TEST SKIPPED, the second attempt running to produce no usable number after the unstandardized 7/6 30/30, so the clearance gate is still undefined; it moves to Thu 7/30 after the hop test, and with the single-leg raise skipped it is now the only left-versus-right datum the week will produce. scienceReviews.changes: 1) Reintroduce loaded soleus work on Wednesday. Seated Calf Raise (HSR) 3x10 at 135 lb goes onto Wed 8/5, replacing that day's bodyweight seated raise rather than adding to it. This is not a new load: 7/28 ran 3x10 at 90/135/135 and it was tolerated. Upper day is the right slot because nothing else there loads the lower leg. That takes genuinely loaded calf work from 1x/week to 2x/week (Wed seated soleus, Fri single-leg gastroc) against Beyer 2015's 3x/week, with the third session to be added next week if the morning reads hold. Tempo 3 s up, 3 s down, floor range, full plantarflexion to neutral, no bottom-end stretch. 2) Take the seated-calf load question to the PT. The daily bodyweight 3x15 is a PT prescription and stays; the coach's loaded HSR session is additive to their program, not a replacement for it. But the 1.5x BW knee-flexed benchmark cannot be built at bodyweight, so ask them directly what the plan is for reloading the soleus, and whether they object to a loaded seated HSR twice weekly on top of the daily block. This is the same open item as 7/27's change 6 and it should not survive another review. 3) Fix the nutrition anchor days. Moderate-deficit days move from Mon/Thu/Sat to Tue/Wed/Sat. Tue is now a rest day with the PT block only, Wed is upper-only with no lower-body demand (the exact rationale that used to justify Thursday), and Sat stays the pre-Sunday-game rest day. Mon and Thu carry the barbell lower work and the run and go to maintenance, and Sun stays maintenance as the game day. Same 3-day structure and the same Helms 2014 logic (PMID 24864135), applied to the schedule that actually exists. 4) Hold Sunday AM basketball one more week, opening 8/16. The two tested criteria are met but the Phase 4 list also requires a completed symptom-free plyo and change-of-direction exposure, which is what Thursday's run and Friday's box jumps are. Already written into the Week 22 plan. 5) Run the capacity test to true failure next time, and record hop height difference between legs, so the asymmetry half of the gate produces a real number instead of a stop-at-target one. 6) Get a body-comp reading this week. Third consecutive review asking. 53 days blind across the highest-regain-risk window the program has had. 7) Log sleep as one number per night. The morning calf read went from absent to seven consecutive days once it was the only field being asked for, and sleep is the same shape of ask. It currently blinds two of the seven reactive-deload triggers. 8) Target re-horizon is reopened as a decision for Week 24, with the arithmetic stated rather than implied. Two coherent options: extend horizons (TB DL and Squat to 24 months, so 3/2028; Bench to 18 months, so 9/2027) and keep the numbers, or keep the horizons and restate the numbers at something the observed rate supports, roughly TB DL 315x5, Squat 265x5, Bench 205x5. Doing neither leaves three progress bars on the site that the data cannot reach, which is the manufactured-progress failure mode. Athlete's call, not the coach's. Near-term milestones either way: reclaim TB DL 245 and Squat 160, the pre-injury peaks, then reassess. 9) No deload signal. Week 24 (8/16 to 8/22) stays a contingency rather than a command per Coleman 2024 (PMID 38274324), with the caveat that the no-fatigue call rests on missing sleep data. Next review: end of Week 23 (Sat 8/15), or immediately if Thursday's run or Friday's box jumps produce a symptom or a next-morning escalation.

21.title: Barbell lower restart, criteria-gated
21.subtitle: Barbell lower restarted Tuesday at the reduced load and went clean. Both gate tests now land Thursday: the hop criteria that gate running, plyos, and Sunday basketball, then the standardized calf-capacity re-test as the session finisher.
21.reason: Week 21 carries the first barbell-lower session since 6/18 - 39 days without TB DL or back squat, and day 36 post-strain. Three facts reshaped the block: basketball is in its off-season so the Tuesday game is gone; Sunday AM basketball stays self-gated until the calf clears; and Weeks 19-20 were travel with little or no training logged. Only one game is on the calendar (hockey Sun 8/2 PM), so the in-season lower-body volume constraint in Section 3 - written for a three-game week - largely lifts. This is the best lower-body rebuild window the program has had. RESTART LOADS are cut ~15% (TB DL 245 to 205, squat 160 to 135). Training cessation lowers every component of muscular strength with a dose-response on cessation duration: maximal force SMD -0.46, submaximal strength -0.62, maximal power -0.20 across 103 studies, with smaller losses in recreational athletes than in inactive people (Bosquet et al. 2013, Scand J Med Sci Sports, PMID 23347054, DOI 10.1111/sms.12047; Moderate). The meta-analysis reports standardized effect sizes, not percentage loss by cessation duration, so the 15% figure is a judgment call from the effect direction, not a number the paper supplies. Two clean sessions earn +10 on lower compounds per the standard double-progression rule. BARBELL LOWER IS NOT THE CALF RISK HERE - plyos, jumps, sprinting, and sport change-of-direction are. TB DL is hip-dominant, and the squat's bottom position has the knee flexed, which slackens the biarticular gastroc: the opposite of the injury mechanism, sudden knee extension with the ankle dorsiflexed (Dixon 2009 PMID 19468870). So barbell lower comes back now while jumps and plyos stay frozen behind the Phase 3 hop gate. Rebuilding strength is itself the protection - a residual capacity deficit is the recurrence substrate, and age 40 plus a prior calf injury is the highest-risk band (Green 2017 PMID 28259848; Green 2022 PMID 35032233). TWO GATE TESTS THIS WEEK, because 'until the calf is 100%' is currently undefined and therefore has no exit. Mon: standardized single-leg calf-raise capacity, both legs, full height and set cadence - the 7/6 result of 30/30 met the rep count but came at lower height and force on the injured left, so the asymmetry half was never confirmed. Thu: roughly 20 symptom-free single-leg hops per leg plus hop asymmetry, the Phase 3 criterion that gates running, step-down plyometrics, and a return to basketball (Green 2022; norms Hebert-Losier 2017 PMID 28886865). Thursday's placement also yields a Friday-morning read that informs the Sunday hockey decision. PAIN RULE throughout: up to 5/10 during loading and next morning, must settle to baseline within 24 h, must not climb week to week (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888; biasing conservative given the bilateral Achilles tendinopathy). No static end-range calf stretching - the 7/6 curb stretch produced a sharp pain shot, and end-range dorsiflexion stretch stays contraindicated. UPDATE 7/29: the week ran a day behind. Monday was rest, so the lower restart moved to Tuesday PM, preceded by a morning PT session for the calf that was treatment only, with no testing and no change to what is cleared. TB DL landed a clean 4x5x205, which is the expected result rather than a surprise: strength decays far more slowly than muscle size, so the first sessions back usually go better than they feel like they will (Psilander et al. 2019, J Appl Physiol 126:1636-45, PMID 30991013, where 20 weeks of detraining returned CSA to baseline while strength stayed roughly 60% elevated; Moderate). Note that the same trial found a previously trained leg did NOT retrain faster than an untrained one, so this is strength retention, not muscle memory. One clean session is banked and a second earns +10 to 215. Do not stack a deload on the far side of the layoff, because the layoff already was one. The calf was silent through the session and read 1-2/10 diffuse on Wednesday morning, well inside the pain rule. THE CAPACITY TEST WAS SKIPPED, the second attempt running that produced no usable number after the unstandardized 7/6 read, so 'when is the calf cleared' still has no defined answer. It moves to Thursday rather than slipping another week, placed after the hop test and as the session finisher, because a to-fatigue test run first would corrupt the hop read. The pre-fatigue cuts one way only: clearing 30 reps per side at 10% or less asymmetry after roughly 20 hops is conservative and settles the gate, while a near-miss is ambiguous and earns a clean re-test on a rested calf. Wednesday's HSR sets come off the board to keep the calf quiet for those tests, and calf loading still happens three times this week (Tue HSR, Thu gate tests, Fri HSR), preserving the Beyer 2015 3x/week frequency. FURTHER UPDATE 7/29: the full Tuesday session came out in pieces and was larger and more divergent than first reported. Back squat was pulled forward from Friday (45/95/135 ramp then 135 held, so two working sets at the restart load and not a clean 4x5), meaning both barbell lower lifts restarted in the same session after a 40-day layoff. Isometric standing calf holds were added (6x30s bilateral plus 3x30s per leg single-leg, 4.5 min of total hold time), seated calf raises ran 3x10 at 90/135/135 rather than 3x8 at 135, and BOTH the loaded single-leg calf raise and the hamstring work were skipped. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the first read of this session: the isometric holds were PT-PRESCRIBED, part of a home program from the morning visit, not freelanced, so the calf additions are clinician-directed and the PT has in fact given rehab-progression guidance. Isometrics are the Phase 1 modality in the consensus progression (Green 2022 PMID 35032233), and collagen signaling tracks strain magnitude rather than contraction type (Kjaer 2009; Magnusson and Kjaer 2019). The single-leg holds also do expose left versus right qualitatively, so an earlier note claiming the session produced no left-right information at all was too strong. What a bodyweight hold cannot do is reach the >=1.0x BW knee-extended strain of BW+25 loaded work or produce a countable rep number, so neither gate criterion is satisfied by it. Do not lean on isometric analgesia either: Rio's findings are patellar-specific and Achilles replication is mixed (Rio 2015 PMID 25979840; Weak for the Achilles generalization). THE PT'S FULL HOME PROGRAM IS NOW RECORDED at athlete.clinicalWorkupAsks.acuteCalfInjuryJun2026.ptHomeProgram, and it restructures the rest of the block. Daily: both isometric hold blocks, seated calf raise 3x15, and step-backs off a small box with a forward chest lean. Two to three times weekly: squats, which the PT already knew about, and single-leg dumbbell RDL 3x8 per leg. The PT knows the full lifting program including the 135 lb seated calf raise and the BW+25 single-leg raise, so this was written on top of it rather than in ignorance of it. Three consequences follow. The program's 3x/week seated calf HSR at 135 RETIRES in favor of the PT's daily 3x15, which is performed UNWEIGHTED (confirmed 7/29, after the program briefly assumed a 90 lb anchor that was never prescribed), making this a real de-load of loaded calf capacity rather than a like-for-like swap; daily calf loading is a legitimate pattern, closer to Alfredson's daily model than to Beyer's 3x/week HSR, and the two produced equivalent 12- and 52-week outcomes (Beyer 2015; Strong). The single-leg RDL replaces both the Glute-Ham Raise and the Bulgarian split squat. And the daily step-backs are controlled stair-descent loading, which supersedes the program's own earlier gate of no heel drop below neutral until stair descent is pain-free: that restriction was the program's, the PT's judgment is more current, and theirs governs. WEDNESDAY'S CALF REST DAY IS THEREFORE CANCELLED, since with a daily prescription there is no rest day left to give. UPDATE 7/30: THE GATE TESTS ARE POSTPONED AGAIN, the fourth slip, this time on a real signal rather than by drift. Thursday's morning read came in at 3-5/10 DOMS across both lower legs, up from 1-2/10 on Tuesday and Wednesday. Roughly 20 SYMPTOM-FREE hops per leg cannot be assessed at 3-5/10, and a to-fatigue capacity test would under-read while adding load three days before hockey, so a number nobody could trust is worse than no number. The soreness itself is unremarkable and reassuring in character: diffuse and bilateral tracks the newly introduced daily program rather than the left strain site, and step-backs were never started, so the stimulus was Tuesday PM, with Wednesday's calf work light by comparison (isometrics plus unweighted seated raises). The timing fits a single-session DOMS curve rather than an escalating trend: Tuesday PM was the big stimulus, Wednesday's calf work was light (isometrics plus BODYWEIGHT raises), and 1-2/10 at 24 h then 3-5/10 at 48 h is the standard delayed-onset pattern, since DOMS peaks 24-72 h after the stimulus and comes from mechanical microtrauma plus inflammation rather than from anything accumulating (knowledge/recovery-sleep.md). That predicts the read IMPROVES by Friday and Saturday rather than climbing further. To bring it down faster before Monday's tests, massage or a percussion gun has the largest effect size among recovery modalities, ahead of active recovery, compression, and cold water immersion, with stretching null (Dupuy 2018; Guo 2017 PMID 29021762; Strong). It is still a week-to-week climb, which the pain model says should not happen, so Thursday adds nothing to the calf (isometrics stay, the seated raise runs unweighted as it always has, step-backs stay unstarted) and picks up Wednesday's skipped pulling and core work instead. Friday's calf items are gated on Friday morning's read. Both tests move to Mon 8/3, which is why Week 22 now exists rather than being written later: an unbuilt week is how this test slipped in the first place. Friday absorbs the rest of the consequences: it becomes squat session 2 aiming for a clean 4x5x135 rather than a restart, and it picks up the skipped single-leg calf raise and hamstring work. The 1-2/10 morning read remains a good tolerance signal for a session that size, with the honest caveat that with this many simultaneous deviations a bad read could not have been pinned on any single one of them.

schedule.longDesc: GATE TESTS POSTPONED, the fourth slip, and this time for a reason rather than an oversight. This morning's read is 3-5/10 DOMS across both lower legs, up from 1-2/10 on Tuesday and Wednesday. The hop criterion is roughly 20 SYMPTOM-FREE single-leg hops per leg, which simply cannot be assessed at 3-5/10, and a to-fatigue capacity test would under-read while adding load three days before hockey. A number you cannot trust is worse than no number. The soreness itself is unremarkable: diffuse and bilateral tracks the newly introduced daily program rather than the left strain site, and step-backs have not even been started, so the stimulus was Tuesday PM, with Wednesday's calf work light by comparison (isometrics plus unweighted seated raises). The timing fits a single-session DOMS curve rather than an escalating trend: Tuesday PM was the big stimulus, Wednesday's calf work was light (isometrics plus BODYWEIGHT raises), and 1-2/10 at 24 h then 3-5/10 at 48 h is the standard delayed-onset pattern, since DOMS peaks 24-72 h after the stimulus and comes from mechanical microtrauma plus inflammation rather than from anything accumulating (knowledge/recovery-sleep.md). That predicts the read IMPROVES by Friday and Saturday rather than climbing further. To bring it down faster before Monday's tests, massage or a percussion gun has the largest effect size among recovery modalities, ahead of active recovery, compression, and cold water immersion, with stretching null (Dupuy 2018; Guo 2017 PMID 29021762; Strong). But it IS a week-to-week climb, and the pain-monitoring model says pain must not increase across weeks (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888), so today reduces calf load rather than adding to it. Isometric holds stay, the seated calf raise runs unweighted as it actually has been, and step-backs stay unstarted until a morning read comes in under 3/10. On the seated raise the program was wrong twice over: it invented a 90 lb anchor and then a 70 lb reduction off it, when the dose being performed is bodyweight. The rest of the day picks up Wednesday's skipped pulling and core work, which is calf-free. Tests move to Mon 8/3, run before that day's PT block, and gated on two consecutive morning reads under 3/10.

The single-leg RDL enters here as the PT's 2-3x weekly item, replacing the Glute-Ham Raise and Bulgarian split squat: hip-dominant, single-leg, calf-sparing, and it exposes left versus right. The BW+25 loaded single-leg calf raise runs once weekly on this day, since it is the only thing in either program that reaches the >=1.0x BW knee-extended benchmark and the PT did not include it. The squat itself is not in question even on sore calves, since the squat bottom has the knee flexed and slackens the biarticular gastroc. THE CALF WORK HERE IS GATED ON FRIDAY MORNING'S READ, because Thursday's read climbed to 3-5/10 and the gate tests were postponed for it. The squat bottom has the knee flexed, which slackens the biarticular gastroc - the opposite of the injury mechanism of knee extension with the ankle dorsiflexed (Dixon 2009 PMID 19468870) - so it is far less provocative than a straight-knee heel drop, but earn full depth back rather than forcing it.

22.title: Gate tests, finally
22.subtitle: Both gate tests passed Monday, first attempt after four slips. Running returns Thursday and box jumps Friday if the morning reads hold. Sunday AM basketball stays held one more week.
22.reason: Monday answered the question this week existed to answer. Both gate tests ran fresh, before the PT block and before any lifting, and both passed: 20 symptom-free single-leg hops per leg, and 30 single-leg calf raises on each leg at 0 percent inter-limb asymmetry against a 10 percent ceiling (Green 2022 PMID 35032233; norms Hebert-Losier 2017 PMID 28886865). Tuesday morning then read calm, roughly 24 h after the largest neuromuscular calf demand since the 6/21 strain, which satisfies the 24-hour rule (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888). Day 43 post-strain, inside the week 5-9 Phase 3 anchor, so on schedule rather than ahead of it. One caveat is worth carrying forward: both legs stopped at exactly 30, the criterion value, on a test specified to fatigue, so that 0 percent probably reflects stopping at the target rather than both legs failing on the same rep. Both criteria are met either way and 30 is a floor, but run it to true failure next time so the weaker leg actually gets identified. Thursday takes the first graded run since the strain, run first while fresh, plus TB DL stepping to 215 off two clean 4x5 sessions at 205. Friday takes the first step-down box jumps since 6/18, gated on a Friday morning read under 3/10 rather than simply scheduled, which is the gating that worked on 7/31. Two novel items on consecutive days is the aggressive part of this week, and the gate is what keeps it honest. Sunday AM basketball holds one more week. The two tested criteria are met, but Green 2022's return-to-sport list also wants the loaded strength benchmarks and a completed symptom-free plyo and change-of-direction exposure, and that exposure is exactly what Thursday and Friday are; clean through both opens basketball on 8/16. The gap to raise with the PT is the other half of those benchmarks, 1.0x BW knee-extended and 1.5x BW knee-flexed. At roughly 220 lb the soleus number is about 330 lb, and the PT's seated calf raise sits at bodyweight for 3x15, which will not build toward it. That is a question for them, not a load to change unilaterally. Wednesday fixes the volume holes carried in from Week 21, where back sat at 5 sets and core at zero direct sets for two straight weeks because 7/30 was skipped entirely. The lat pulldown, the woodchop and the Pallof press all come back, putting back at 8 sets and core at 6, which clears the 4-6 core floor. The pain rule is unchanged: up to 5/10 during loading and the next morning, settling to baseline within 24 h, and not climbing week to week (Silbernagel 2007). And passing a gate is not discharge. Age and prior calf injury are the two strongest recurrence risk factors (Green 2017 PMID 28259848) and recurrence in this band arrives without warning, so calf-raise capacity is a permanent maintenance item now.

Recurrence in this band often arrives without warning (Green 2017 PMID 28259848), which is what the warm-up and the stop rule are for. Log how the calf handled it, and Monday morning's read decides whether the gate tests run.

Capacity: 30 left and 30 right, clearing the 30-rep threshold at 0 percent inter-limb asymmetry against a 10 percent ceiling (Green 2022 PMID 35032233). Worth keeping in mind, though: both legs stopped at exactly 30 on a test specified to fatigue, so that 0 percent is more likely a stop-at-target than a true failure read. TB DL 4x5x205 clean, the second consecutive clean session at 205, which opens 215. Single-leg RDL 3x8/leg at 20 lb DBs. Seated calf raise and step-backs were held by design on a test day. Whether the isometric block ran after the tests was not reported.

exercises.name: Single-leg hop test (gate)
exercises.notes: Run first. Start with small submaximal hops in place, build height only while symptom-free. Record hops completed per leg, any symptom and where it appeared, and the height difference between sides. Targets: roughly 20 symptom-free hops and 10% or less hop asymmetry. Don't push through sharp pain; stop and log it. ROM: land midfoot with a soft knee, no forced heel contact.

exercises.notes: Second, after the hops, and before any lifting. Full height every rep, roughly 2 s per rep cadence, knee straight, stop when height drops or form breaks. Record reps left and right. Gate is 30 or more reps with 10% or less asymmetry. The 7/6 result of 30/30 does not count: it was unstandardized and the injured left produced less height and force.

This corrects an error in the earlier version of this prescription. 7/28 banked one clean 4x5x205, and double progression requires two consecutive clean sessions at the same load before adding weight (Schoenfeld 2017 PMID 27433992; NSCA Essentials Ch. 18), so today is the second session rather than the payoff for it. A clean 4x5x205 today earns 215 on Thursday. Two more reasons to hold regardless: the hop test and a to-fatigue capacity test run first, so the calf arrives at the bar pre-fatigued, and 7/28 was the first barbell lower in 40 days, where restart loads bias small and a layoff is not a stall (knowledge/detraining-and-return.md; Psilander 2019 PMID 30991013). RPE 6-7. ROM: full range from the floor, heels flat, hips loaded.

Dropped in the shift: close-grip bench, both core movements, and the loaded seated calf raise. See the 8/6 activity log for the full read. The original prescription is preserved below. Bench holds 165: 7/29 took four sets at 165 for 3, 5, 3, 3, so one clean set of five out of four attempts. Get all four and 170 opens. Back and core are the real point here. 7/30 was skipped entirely and took the lat pulldown and the woodchop with it, leaving back at 5 sets and core at zero direct sets for a second straight week against a 4-6 set floor. Bringing back the pulldown puts back at 8 sets, and the woodchop plus Pallof press puts core at 6. Overhead press works back up off the empty bar it defaulted to on 7/29, since 45 lb is far below what a seated press should allow off a 95x5 standing base, so 65 is a rebuild step rather than a progression. The row steps to 105 for the same reason: 95 sits 40 lb under the last clean pre-layoff set. The press stays seated on purpose so there is no leg drive and no plantarflexion load. One addition out of the Week 22 science review: the loaded seated calf raise comes back at 135, replacing today's bodyweight version. Calf loading has gone daily but entirely at bodyweight, so frequency has been masking an intensity failure, and the Phase 4 soleus benchmark of roughly 1.5x BW cannot be built on 3x15 unweighted. 135 is not a new load; 7/28 tolerated it. Confirm with the PT.

schedule.desc: Upper ran AM, run and lower PM
schedule.longDesc: DOUBLE SESSION. Wednesday's upper day was skipped and ran this morning instead, so the run and lower work below move to the evening. That changes one prescription: TB DL holds 205 rather than stepping to 215, for attribution rather than fatigue. Friday's box jumps are gated on a Friday morning read under 3/10 with no escalation off today's run (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888). With an AM upper session, a first run in 46 days and a new deadlift load all landing on the same day, a bad Friday read would have three candidate causes and the gate becomes uninterpretable. 205 has gone clean twice and costs nothing to repeat, so holding it leaves the run as the only novel variable. The 215 step moves to Monday, where it is still earned. The run is the session. First running since the 6/21 strain, 46 days, unlocked by Monday's 20 symptom-free hops per leg (Green 2022 PMID 35032233 gates running on the hop test). Run first, before the barbell work, because it is the novel stimulus and a fatigued first run measures fatigue rather than tolerance. This morning's upper session does not compromise that: bench and rows leave the calf untouched, and the systemic cost of seven upper sets is small against a 6-minute jog. The dose is a coaching call, not a protocol: Green 2022 names graded return to running as a phase without prescribing a dose, so the interval structure below is a conservative extrapolation and should be read as one. Flat, level ground, easy conversational pace, no hills, no sprints, no cutting. A running mechanism predicted longer return-to-play in the AFL cohort (Green 2020 PMID 33030961), which is the reason to start this small rather than jog for 20 minutes because the gate opened. Then the barbell work: TB DL steps to 215 off two clean 4x5 sessions at 205 (7/28 and 8/3), the compound-lower double progression working normally for the first time since the restart. Squat holds 135 as the PT's 2-3x weekly item, first squat of the week. Friday morning's read is the datum that matters, since it decides whether Friday's box jumps go, under the 24-hour rule (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888).

The box jumps are gated, not scheduled: they go only if this morning's calf read is under 3/10 and Thursday's run produced no next-morning escalation. 16.reason: Sun 6/21 AM basketball: a minor right-calf pull was played through, then minutes later an acute severe left-calf strain - the textbook 'tennis leg' (acute medial gastrocnemius strain; Delgado 2002 PMID 12091669; Dixon 2009 PMID 19468870). Difficulty bearing weight since = at least Grade II. The #1 priority is an IN-PERSON exam before any programming: rule out Achilles rupture via the Thompson/Simmonds squeeze test (the critical miss - rupture patients can still walk and weakly plantarflex; Boyd 2015 PMID 26622031; Maffulli 1998 PMID 9548122), assess DVT (~10% of tennis-leg; Wells 1997 PMID 9428249), and seek emergency care if pain is out of proportion with a tense compartment. Acute care = PEACE then LOVE (Dubois & Esculier 2020 PMID 31377722): protect, elevate, compression, education; short-course ibuprofen for pain is fine (Morelli 2018 PMID 28355084) but transition to acetaminophen as pain eases and don't run NSAIDs for weeks. Early protected loading beats immobilization (Jarvinen 2005 PMID 15851777; Bayer 2017 PMID 28953439), so gentle pain-free ROM starts now and pain-free isometrics late this week. HSR is de-loaded to zero and rebuilt later - NOT continued at the pre-injury 155 lb / BW+72 loads. Recurrence risk is high (age + prior calf injury are the top risk factors; Green 2017 PMID 28259848), so the whole block is criteria-gated.

Progress isometrics -> double-leg -> single-leg calf raises through a tolerable range, and REINTRODUCE HSR at a markedly reduced load (rebuild, do not resume the pre-injury 155 lb seated / BW+72 single-leg loads). The rehab trajectory and the Achilles tendinopathy plan are the same progressive-loading trajectory, so they reconverge here (Beyer 2015 PMID 26018970 as the loading substrate; transfer to acute strain is Moderate/extrapolated). Pain rule throughout (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888): <=5/10 during/next-morning, no week-to-week increase; bias conservative. No games this week - calf strains recur 'without warning' and the priority order is injury prevention first. | 6/29 REVIEW UPDATE: calf is improving but at the LOAD CEILING - morning-after pain lingers (the 24h return-to-baseline rule is not cleanly met) and stair descent plus occasional sharp steps still hurt (eccentric gastroc reactivity). HOLD rehab load this week; gate any increase (the Wed/Fri steps, single-leg progression, soleus loading) on the next-morning pain FIRST returning to baseline. WHAT YOU CAN STILL TRAIN to limit detraining: upper body (as the 6/25 session) plus calf-SPARING lower isolation - seated leg extension, hip thrust / glute bridge, back extension (bent knee + quiet ankle = minimal gastroc demand). HOLD all calf-loading compounds until Phase 2: back squat, deadlift incl. trap bar, leg press, lunges / split squats, heavy leg curls, and all jumping / running. The gastroc is biarticular - a loaded squat stretches it at depth and a deadlift loads it under heavy axial drive, which is too much at ~day 8 of a Grade I-II strain. Recurrence risk is highest at 40 with a calf injury now on record (Green 2017 PMID 28259848; Green 2020 PMID 33030961) - do not load on feel.

18.title: Calf: Phase 2 strength and monitored return to games
18.subtitle: Confirm-and-protect: measure single-leg capacity, keep loading the calf, watch the morning-after read after games. Barbell lower stays frozen until the capacity gate clears.
18.reason: Wk 18 pivots from linear rehab to CONFIRM-AND-PROTECT after the athlete returned to hockey off-plan on Sun 7/5 (day 14) and tolerated it - light morning-after soreness that subsided within the 24-hour window (Silbernagel 2007 PMID 17307888), a pass that beats the 6/29 lingering pattern. That clears the gate the prior review waited on, so cautious continued play is defensible and games are the A-priority (no longer withheld). BUT the return jumped ahead of the objective RTS gates, which remain UNTESTED: single-leg calf-raise capacity >=30 reps and inter-limb asymmetry <=10%, plus loaded strength toward >=1.0x BW knee-extended and >=1.5x BW knee-flexed soleus (Green 2022 PMID 35032233; Hebert-Losier 2017 PMID 28886865). A capacity/strength deficit can persist while pain is gone, and that deficit is the recurrence substrate - recurrence is frequent, 'without warning,' and highest in his band (age 40 + prior calf injury; Green 2017 PMID 28259848; Green 2020 PMID 33030961). So this week does three things at once: (1) MEASURE - get the single-leg capacity/asymmetry number early, fresh (the one hard datum still missing); (2) LOAD - keep building calf strength, gastroc (knee-straight) + soleus (bent-knee) HSR rebuilding toward but not past the pre-injury loads, because loading out the deficit is the active protection against recurrence, more than rest is; (3) MONITOR - log pain-during and pain-next-morning after every game/hard session; light-and-subsiding = keep going, lingering-or-climbing = pull back to loaded rehab that week. De-risk each game: thorough calf warm-up, ease into maximal push-off, stop on any sharp calf pain. Lower-body BARBELL lifts (TB DL, squat) stay FROZEN until the capacity gate clears and mornings stay clean. Pain rule throughout: <=5/10 during and next-morning, settle in 24h, no week-to-week increase; bias conservative given the bilateral Achilles-tendinopathy context. Full evidence: knowledge/calf-strain-rehab.md.
